behavioral_notes.observation: The Odoo server acts as a CORS proxy for the POS JS client: proxy_adyen_request validates the incoming SaleToPOIRequest structure against an allowlist of permitted request shapes (payment, cancel/abort, capture, adjust) using a recursive _is_valid_adyen_request_data validator with a UNPREDICTABLE_ADYEN_DATA sentinel for dynamic fields. Only whitelisted shapes are forwarded to https://terminal-api-{live|test}.adyen.com/async. For payment requests, the server injects a pos_hmac HMAC (odoo.tools.hmac, scope='pos_adyen_payment', message=(SaleID, ServiceID, POIID, TransactionID)) into SaleToAcquirerData before forwarding — this HMAC is later used to authenticate the Adyen webhook response.

The public webhook endpoint receives asynchronous SaleToPOIResponse messages from Adyen's cloud terminal API. It validates the HMAC from AdditionalResponse (metadata.pos_hmac) via consteq against the re-computed HMAC, then strips the HMAC from the payload before storing it. The response JSON is written to adyen_latest_response on pos.payment.method, and pos.session notifies the POS frontend via pos_bus (_notify('ADYEN_LATEST_RESPONSE', config_id)). The endpoint unconditionally returns '[accepted]' to satisfy Adyen's cloud webhook guarantee requirement.

The POS frontend patches PosStore.setup to subscribe to the WebSocket event ADYEN_LATEST_RESPONSE via data.connectWebSocket. On receipt, it calls handleAdyenStatusResponse on the pending Adyen payment line's terminal object. That method calls get_latest_adyen_status (ORM RPC) to fetch the buffered JSON from adyen_latest_response, validates the ServiceID matches the pending line's terminalServiceId, then resolves a Promise stored in paymentLineResolvers[line.uuid] — or falls back to line.handlePaymentResponse(). This is a split async flow: JS initiates payment -> Python proxies to Adyen -> Adyen calls webhook -> bus event -> JS resolves the pending Promise.

When adyen_ask_customer_for_tip is enabled, a @api.constrains validator enforces that tip_product_id and iface_tipproduct are also configured on the POS config — raising ValidationError otherwise. On the JS side, _adyenPayData includes SaleToAcquirerData='tenderOption=AskGratuity' in the payment request, and handleSuccessResponse reads TipAmount from AmountsResp.TipAmount and calls pos.setTip(tip_amount) + line.setAmount(AuthorizedAmount). The tip flow therefore spans Python config validation, a request-time field in SaleToAcquirerData, and a response-time ORM call — none of this is visible in metadata.

pos_adyen overrides _is_write_forbidden to exclude adyen_latest_response from the write-forbidden set. This allows the webhook handler to buffer the asynchronous Adyen notification (adyen_latest_response) even when the POS session is in a state that would normally block writes to the payment method record — a deliberate carve-out to support the async notification buffering pattern.

it_architecture.application: pos_adyen (Adyen Terminal API integration for Odoo POS — cloud async architecture)
data_objects: pos.payment.method (extended: adyen_api_key, adyen_terminal_identifier, adyen_test_mode, adyen_latest_response, adyen_event_url)
information_flows: POS JS -> proxy_adyen_request (ORM RPC) -> Python CORS proxy (HMAC injection) -> Adyen terminal-api-{env}.adyen.com/async
Adyen -> /pos_adyen/notification (HMAC-validated webhook) -> adyen_latest_response buffer -> pos_bus ADYEN_LATEST_RESPONSE -> POS JS WebSocket -> Promise resolution
frontend_components: PaymentAdyen (extends PaymentInterface, registered as 'adyen' payment method)
Patches: PosStore.prototype (WebSocket subscription), PaymentScreen.prototype (pending line recovery on mount), PosPayment.prototype (terminalServiceId field)

capabilities: Process card payments at POS via Adyen physical terminal (cloud async flow)
Support customer tipping on terminal (AskGratuity tenderOption)
Buffer and validate asynchronous Adyen payment notifications via webhook
Enforce unique terminal assignment across payment methods and companies
value_streams: POS Payment: cashier selects Adyen payment -> JS sends request via Odoo proxy to Adyen terminal -> customer taps card -> Adyen sends webhook -> bus event resolves JS promise -> payment line marked done -> order closed
policies: Terminal identifier must be unique per company (ValidationError on _check_adyen_terminal_identifier)
Tipping requires tip_product_id and iface_tipproduct on pos.config (ValidationError on _check_adyen_ask_customer_for_tip)
proxy_adyen_request requires point_of_sale.group_pos_user or superuser; only allowlisted request shapes are forwarded
Webhook HMAC validated via consteq before processing; HMAC stripped from stored payload
stakeholders: POS Manager (configures Adyen API key and terminal identifier)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_adyen is a primary-activity chain module: it closes the payment step of the point-of-sale value chain by connecting the order-taking activity directly to card acceptance at a physical terminal, enabling revenue capture.

standard_capabilities: Cloud async Adyen Terminal API (Nexo Retailer Protocol 3.0) payment flow
CORS proxy (proxy_adyen_request) with request-shape whitelist and HMAC injection
Public webhook receiver with HMAC validation and pos_bus notification
Customer tipping on terminal with tip product constraint
Test/live environment switching per payment method
typical_fits: Standard brick-and-mortar POS with Adyen Verifone/Castles terminal
Cloud architecture: no local network required between POS and terminal
common_gaps: No local terminal API (LOCALHOST) support — cloud only
No offline/fallback when Adyen cloud is unreachable
No refund flow via terminal (refunds handled externally or via Adyen dashboard)
Webhook URL must be manually pasted into Adyen portal (adyen_event_url field is informational)
drive_hints: curl -X POST /pos_adyen/notification with a SaleToPOIResponse JSON to test webhook parsing

open_questions: Does pos_adyen support local terminal API (LOCALHOST mode) or only Adyen cloud async?
How does the payment flow behave on POS session reconnect if adyen_latest_response contains a stale notification from a previous session?
Is there a refund path through the terminal, or are refunds entirely out-of-band?
